title: Grateful Dead Live at Electric Factory on 1969-02-15
lineage: Cassette (Nakamichi Dragon) > DAT (Panasonic SV-3800/48k) DAT (Sony PCM-R700) > Sound Forge > CD > FLAC
taper: Master Reel > Cassette by Dick Latvala Cassette > DAT by Rob Eaton DAT > CD by Jim Wise

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1969 show captured on a soundboard remaster with solid audio and a standout (though possibly incomplete) The Eleven.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the electrifying performance, noting that the recording—derived from an original first‑generation cassette of the soundboard—is surprisingly clear and rivals some of the era’s best shows. While there are concerns that The Eleven may have been trimmed on the source tape, the overall musical quality is praised as high.

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviewers gave 4‑5 stars and highlighted strong show performance; recording is decent but limited by cassette source and potential cuts, leading to a solid but not perfect rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: First‑generation cassette copy shows some tape hiss and possible cuts (notably in The Eleven), but the remaster is clear enough to be enjoyable and rivals top recordings of the period.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Specific set details are sparse, but reviewers feel the performance flows strongly and stands among the best of the era.
